summary.title: How to pick more beautiful colors for your data visualizations
summary.one_liner: Learn practical color rules for categorical data visualizations, such as using a few neighboring hues, adjusting saturation and lightness, and keeping backgrounds desaturated.
takeaways: Stick to a few neighboring hues on the color wheel and use complementary pairs when unsure.
Vary saturation and lightness so categorical colors remain distinguishable in grayscale and for colorblind readers.
Avoid pure hues (multiples of 60°) and 100% saturation/brightness; desaturate or darken them.
Use warm colors with blue as a versatile categorical pair, and make greens leaning yellow or blue.
Keep chart backgrounds desaturated: light backgrounds above 95% lightness, dark ones below 20% saturation.
summary.summary: Datawrapper's Lisa Charlotte Muth walks through common color mistakes in data visualization and how to fix them. The article explains HSB/HSV and HCL color spaces, then gives numbered rules on hue selection, saturation and lightness, contrast with backgrounds, and greens. It uses many illustrative color examples (mostly as images, which the text does not describe) and links to tools such as Paletton, Adobe Color, and colorizer.org. It closes with advice on copying and analyzing colors from images and existing visualizations.
